title: From Small Talk to Rapport: Exploring Robot Self-Disclosure in Collaborative Tasks
one_sentence: During a short physical co-working task, a low-disclosure industrial manipulator elicited more user disclosure and stronger teaming/coordination ratings than a high-disclosure version.
problem: How should non-anthropomorphic robots use self-disclosure in small talk while performing physical work with people?
method: A between-subjects study with 50 participants compared low- and high-disclosure GPT-4o dialogue strategies on a Franka Panda during an approximately 17-minute loosely coupled sorting task, using coded conversational behavior, surveys, and interviews.
findings: Users in the high-disclosure condition showed lower turn-level disclosure, while direct robot prompts increased disclosure in both conditions.
Low disclosure produced higher perceived teaming and rapport-coordination; prior robot-teaming experience moderated several outcomes.
Interviews suggest embodiment incongruence, perceived inauthenticity, shallow reciprocity, and privacy concerns as plausible explanations, not established mediators.
real_contribution: Provides a non-obvious embodied HRI boundary: adding socially richer content can undermine rather than improve relational and coordination outcomes when signal content, platform form, authenticity, and privacy expectations conflict.
biggest_weakness: The manipulation changed both disclosure content and robot word count, relied on fictional prior-conversation material, used stepwise AIC models with many covariates in N=50, and did not causally isolate the proposed mechanisms.
claim_boundary: Supports a short-term, single-platform self-disclosure effect and qualitative mechanism hypotheses; it does not establish adaptive communication, common ground, convention formation, or broad non-anthropomorphic-robot generalization.
why_researcher_should_care: It shows that instrumental embodiment and relational language can interact non-monotonically, motivating designs that measure authenticity, privacy, reciprocity, and task coordination rather than assuming more social signaling is better.

amsc.master_list_decision: Candidate — Important / social–functional embodied communication boundary

evidence_notes: Open arXiv PDF inspected; v1 submitted 2026-08-28.
Interview explanations are retained as plausible interpretations rather than causal findings.
